subjective_pass_disagreements.expectation: Mentions the rungs/options in terms of effort for the platform versus value delivered, not only feature descriptions

with_skill.expectation: Recommends platform-stored, app-owned namespaced extension fields or objects as the default mechanism for the tracking data
Requires a partner namespace or reserved prefix for the partner's extension definitions
States that partner extension data should be visible only to tenants that installed or authorized that partner
Uses the January peak deadline as a reason favouring the mechanisms that need no partner engineering
Orders removal: partner variant or contract first, then the base graph

without_skill.expectation: Classifies the partner need into a shape before choosing a mechanism (stored data, events, live data, or the partner's own capabilities)
Identifies tracking number and carrier name as stored data the platform can hold, not data that must be computed live by the partner at query time
Recommends platform-stored, app-owned namespaced extension fields or objects as the default mechanism for the tracking data
Names the condition under which a partner-hosted resolver or partner subgraph would become justified (data that must be live and computed by the partner)
Requires a partner namespace or reserved prefix for the partner's extension definitions
States that partner extension data should be visible only to tenants that installed or authorized that partner
Defines what happens to the partner's definitions and values when a tenant uninstalls or the partner leaves
Uses the January peak deadline as a reason favouring the mechanisms that need no partner engineering
Mentions the rungs/options in terms of effort for the platform versus value delivered, not only feature descriptions
Recommends a per-partner credential minted per request (short-lived, audience-bound to the insurer, scoped to tenant) instead of the client token
States that a static header insert in router config cannot carry a per-request tenant-bound token, so a router extension, coprocessor or proxy is needed
Warns that a whole-request router timeout set at or below the partner timeout turns a stalled partner into a failed query instead of partial data
Requires a circuit breaker per partner, or an egress proxy with outlier detection where the router lacks one
Requires the insurer endpoint to authenticate router calls (mTLS or signed platform token) and take tenant from the token, not from the entity representation
Raises `deduplicate_query` or shared caching as a cross-tenant sharing risk for partner responses
Flags `type Money @shareable` as an unprefixed type that merges with or co-resolves the platform's Money type
Ties the @requires concern to a data-clearance list or consent for each field the partner receives
Flags `type Review` and `Query.reviews` as missing a partner namespace/prefix
Recommends a blocking policy check in the platform registry that rejects banned directives on every partner publish, not a manual review comment
Lists @override, @provides and @shareable on platform fields as directives a partner may not use
Notes that the partner itself should not hold publish rights; the platform publishes
States that many self-serve apps make per-partner mapping or per-partner schema review (remote schemas or subgraphs) not scale
Specifies what the mediated field returns (e.g. a platform-defined envelope plus a validated partner payload, or compares envelope vs JSON scalar vs per-partner union)
Hands the field removal to the platform's deprecation/notice window rather than deleting on Friday
Orders removal: partner variant or contract first, then the base graph
Acknowledges that a few contracted partners needing live data joined across several platform entities is the condition that can justify partner subgraphs
Rejects composing partner subgraphs into the main first-party supergraph and requires a separate partner variant or router
Distinguishes what partners must run (a subgraph library, check access) from the platform's router/composition licensing
Includes a blocking policy check on every partner publish in the guide or platform process
Includes an offboarding or removal section in the guide
Notes that @requires ships the required fields once per entity, so a 50-prescription page sends patient data for every row
Requires the partner endpoint to authenticate platform calls and not take tenant from the representation
States that no clinic user credential is forwarded to the partner
Masks partner error messages and does not pass partner response extensions through to clinic clients
Classifies the pricing need as live partner-computed data before specifying the field
